concepts.title: Agent Governance Decision Rights Survey
concepts.research_question: For a specific deployed agent, which roles decide inventory, identity issuance, authorization, budget, monitoring, incident response, decommissioning, legal accountability, and board reporting?
concepts.target_population: Executives and accountable senior operators who made at least one decision about a production or formally piloted tool-using agent in the prior 18 months
concepts.sampling_concern: OFF’s network and event applicants are selective, role lanes are uneven, and multiple respondents may describe the same organization or deployment. There is no probability sampling frame for all executives.
bias_risks: nonresponse by legal and board roles
concepts.analysis_plan: Pre-register exclusions and subgroup floors; deduplicate deployments; report complete bases, missingness, recruitment channel, role and geography composition; describe within-sample distributions; compare roles only with matched question wording and scope; use multilevel or clustered estimates only as exploratory; publish uncertainty and sensitivity analyses without population weights unless a defensible frame exists.
concepts.publication_threshold: At least 300 eligible respondents; at least 40 respondents and 25 organizations in each role used for a headline comparison; at least three regions and four industries; no organization contributes more than two respondents to a role cell; cells below 10 suppressed; no headline without complete base and question wording.
concepts.relationship_to_existing_off_research: Extends OFF’s CISO, CEO, CFO, CMO, and Executive AI Leverage reports by measuring decision ownership for one concrete deployment. Existing mixed-room answers provide questionnaire-development context only and must not be pooled without eligibility and role reconciliation.
claims_the_survey_could_support: Among eligible respondents in a disclosed role and period, the observed distribution of decision ownership
Where responsibility and consultation overlap in the recruited sample
Associations between deployment context and reported governance structure
claims_the_survey_could_not_support: What all executives or enterprises do
Causal effects of a governance model
Regional prevalence from small or convenience cells

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Cross-functional professional association or unrestricted research grant
sponsorship.conflict_risk: A security, IAM, consulting, or platform sponsor could benefit from assigning ownership to its buyer.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Sponsor category, paid relationships, recruitment channels, and OFF ownership.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Instrument and analysis pre-registered before sponsor access; sponsor cannot select roles, questions, or headlines.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: Public aggregates only; no row-level data, contact information, identities, or small cells.
sponsorship.publication_independence: OFF publishes null, adverse, and inconclusive findings on the registered schedule.

concepts.title: Agent Authorization Implementation and Outcomes Registry
concepts.research_question: Which identity, credential, delegation, monitoring, and shutdown patterns are implemented, at what scale, and with what reported failures, burdens, and outcomes?
concepts.target_population: Named technical or control owners able to complete a deployment-level record for a production, pilot, failed, or abandoned agent implementation
concepts.sampling_concern: Successful and vendor-supported deployments are easier to recruit; deployments are heterogeneous; one respondent may lack complete security, cost, and outcome data.
core_measures: monitor false positives and missed events
bias_risks: multiple records for one work or deployment
concepts.analysis_plan: Validate each deployment identity; preserve version and time window; separate reported from independently corroborated outcomes; stratify by autonomy and consequence; report patterns descriptively; compare only records with compatible denominators; include negative and abandoned cases; publish a data dictionary and missingness matrix.
concepts.publication_threshold: At least 120 validated deployment records across 40 organizations, four industries, and three regions; at least 20 failed or abandoned cases; no organization exceeds 10% of records; at least two roles verify 30 matched deployments; claims use deployment-level denominators and corroboration status.
concepts.relationship_to_existing_off_research: Operationalizes the governance and budget questions in OFF’s public reports. It must not treat event demand, applicant answers, or vendor descriptions as implementation outcomes.
claims_the_survey_could_support: Which patterns appear in the validated registry sample
Observed outcome and burden ranges for comparable deployment strata
Documented negative cases and implementation tradeoffs
claims_the_survey_could_not_support: Causal control effectiveness from unrandomized self-reports

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Standards body, audit association, or unrestricted foundation grant
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Vendors may seek pay-to-include visibility or favorable architecture comparisons.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Funding, platform, implementation, and author relationships on every contributed record.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: No pay-to-include; independent eligibility and corroboration review.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: Public deidentified registry and aggregates only; no confidential diagrams or respondent data.
sponsorship.publication_independence: OFF retains failed and unfavorable records subject to rights and correction policy.

concepts.title: Human Approval and Monitor Burden Survey
concepts.research_question: Under which action-risk conditions do human approval, automated monitoring, hard limits, and shutdown controls produce usable oversight rather than delay, consent fatigue, false confidence, or surveillance burden?
concepts.target_population: People who approve, monitor, audit, operate, or are materially affected by a deployed agent workflow, recruited around a specific workflow and recent time window
concepts.sampling_concern: Retrospective perceptions cannot establish causal effectiveness; organizations may not measure missed events; affected users and privacy perspectives are harder to recruit than control owners.
concepts.analysis_plan: Separate retrospective survey from any prospective workflow study; pre-register scenario order and risk strata; report perceived burden separately from logged outcomes; compare roles within the same workflow where possible; adjust for clustered organizations; do not label associations as causal.
concepts.publication_threshold: At least 200 eligible respondents across 30 workflows and 15 organizations; at least 40 respondents in each role used for comparison; at least 10 workflows with matched approver and operator responses; no effectiveness headline without logged denominator from a separately reviewed field-study subset.
concepts.relationship_to_existing_off_research: Tests a question absent from OFF leverage reports: whether governance controls add usable oversight or merely activity. It may use OFF rooms for recruitment, not as an implied representative frame.
claims_the_survey_could_support: Reported burden and practice patterns among the disclosed sample
Hypotheses for a prospective outcome study
claims_the_survey_could_not_support: That approval or monitoring causes safer outcomes
That low burden means effective control

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Monitoring vendors may equate activity with effectiveness or minimize privacy burden.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Independent protocol and analysis; vendor measures cannot define success alone.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No user-level data, workflow logs, or identities to sponsor.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Burden, privacy, null, and adverse findings remain publishable.
